title: Shankar’s International Dolls Museum
content:
Shankar’s Dolls Museum - Delhi,

Shankar’s International Dolls Museum is one of Delhi’s most fascinating museums, established by renowned cartoonist K. Shankar Pillai in 1965. Located inside the Children’s Book Trust building at ITO, the museum houses an extraordinary collection of over 6,000 dolls from 85 different countries, making it a true celebration of world cultures.

The museum is divided into two sections – one showcasing dolls from around the world and the other highlighting Indian dolls dressed in traditional attire from different states. These miniature figures beautifully depict cultural traditions, festivals, and lifestyles. For children, it is not only entertaining but also a learning experience about global diversity.

History of the Museum:

The idea of the Dolls Museum was inspired when Shankar received a doll from a Hungarian diplomat in the 1950s. Over time, he collected dolls during international visits, and soon contributions poured in from across the globe. With the support of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, the museum was officially inaugurated in 1965 and has since become a popular attraction for families and tourists alike.

Visitor Information:

  • Location: Nehru House, Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, ITO, New Delhi.
  • Timings: 10:00 AM – 5:30 PM (Closed on Mondays and national holidays).
  • Entry Fee: ₹20 (Children) | ₹40 (Adults) | Special group discounts available.

How to Reach:

  • By Metro: Nearest metro station is ITO (Violet Line), a short walk from the museum.
  • By Bus/Auto: Well-connected via DTC buses and auto-rickshaws from different parts of Delhi.
  • By Car: Located on Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg with easy access from central Delhi.
  • Parking: Limited parking is available near the museum; visitors are advised to use metro or nearby public parking areas.

Nearby Attractions:

  • National Bal Bhavan – An interactive space for children with workshops and exhibitions.
  • India Gate – A historic war memorial just a short drive away.
  • National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA) – Showcasing India’s modern and contemporary art.

Travel Tips: If you’re visiting with children, plan your trip in the morning hours for a less-crowded and more enjoyable experience.
